'''Leslie Ain McClure''' is an American biostatistician. She is a [[Full professor]] of biostatistics at the [[Drexel University School of Public Health]] and was the inaugural Associate Director of Diversity for the [[Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute]] (2017–18).

==Early life and education==
McClure was born Suffern, New York, and raised in [[Overland Park, Kansas]]. She earned her [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in Mathematics from the [[University of Kansas]]. During high school, she was a member of the marching band which she credits for teaching her a work/life balance.<ref name = "amstat">{{cite web |title=Celebrating Women in Statistics: Leslie McClure |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/01/leslie-mcclure/ |website=magazine.amstat.org |publisher=[[American Statistical Association]] |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=March 1, 2020}}</ref> Upon completing her Bachelor of Science degree, McClure enrolled at the [[University of Iowa]] for her [[Master's degree]] in Preventive Medicine and Environmental Health and then [[University of Michigan]] for her PhD in Biostatistics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leslie McClure, PhD |url=https://www.uab.edu/medicine/diabetes/faculty/faculty-bios/155-leslie-mcclure |website=uab.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon completing her PhD, McClure joined the faculty in the Department of Biostatistics at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]] (UAB).<ref name ="McDonald">{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Sue |title=SAMSI Welcomes Leslie McClure as New Associate Director of Diversity |url=https://www.samsi.info/samsi-welcomes-leslie-mcclure-as-new-associate-director-of-diversity/ |website=samsi.info |publisher=[[Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute]] |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=October 3, 2017}}</ref> During her tenure at the institution, she collaborated with Nalini Sathiakumar to better understand the relationship between environmental conditions observed from space and the health effects experienced on Earth. She used satellite data to measure particulate matter, ozone, and other environmental exposures, which she then used to track the effects of air quality.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Freeman |first1=Laura |title=Satellites for the People |url=https://www.uab.edu/uabmagazine/spring2008/features/satellites |website=uab.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=Spring 2008}}</ref> In 2014, McClure was invited to join the inaugural Edge of Chaos Scholars program which deals with "problems that defy easy or obvious solutions."<ref>{{cite web |title=SOM faculty named among Edge of Chaos Scholars |url=https://www.uab.edu/medicine/news/latest/item/445-som-faculty-named-among-edge-of-chaos-scholars |website=uab.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> The following year, she published a paper using data from the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke ([https://www.uab.edu/soph/regardsstudy/ REGARDS]) study which found that second hand smoke led to an increased risk of stroke by 30 percent.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bakken |first1=Jim |title=Nonsmokers at increased risk of stroke from secondhand smoke |url=https://www.uab.edu/news/research/item/6276-nonsmokers-at-increased-risk-of-stroke-from-secondhand-smoke |website=uab.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=July 9, 2015}}</ref>

After spending 11 years at UAB, McClure left the institution to become the Chair of the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics at the [[Drexel University School of Public Health|Drexel University Dornsife School of Public Health]].<ref name ="McDonald"/><ref name = "Award">{{cite web |title=Leslie Ain McClure receives Janet L. Norwood Award for Outstanding Achievement by a Woman in Statistical Sciences |url=https://www.uab.edu/soph/home/news-events/news/leslie-ain-mcclure-receives-janet-l-norwood-award-for-outstanding-achievement-by-a-woman-in-statistical-sciences |website=uab.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=September 15, 2020}}</ref> At Drexel, McClure leads the Data Coordinating Center for the AJ Drexel Autism Institute's Connecting the Dots Study and is the PI for the Coordinating Center for the CDC-sponsored Diabetes LEAD Network.<ref name ="x">{{cite web |title=Leslie Ain McClure, PhD, MS |url=https://drexel.edu/dornsife/academics/faculty/Leslie%20McClure/ |website=drexel.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref> In 2017, she was appointed the inaugural Associate Director of Diversity for the [[Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute]].,<ref name ="McDonald"/> a position she held for a year. She is also the Chairperson of the Board of Directors for the [[National Alliance for Doctoral Studies in Mathematical Sciences]].

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], McClure was elected a Fellow of the [[Society for Clinical Trials]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 Society for Clinical Trials Fellows Webinar |url=https://drexel.edu/now/events/calendar/details/?eid=30458&iid=81256 |website=drexel.edu |access-date=January 19, 2021 |date=July 8, 2020}}</ref> She is also a Fellow of the [[American Heart Association]] (Epidemiology Council) and a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref name ="x"/> McClure was also the recipient of the Janet L. Norwood Award for Outstanding Achievement by a Woman in Statistical Sciences.<ref name = "Award"/>

==Personal life==
McClure writes a blog called Stat Girl.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barlett |first1=Tom |title='Exhausting.' 'Very Strange.' What It's Like to Be an Epidemiologist Right Now. |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/exhausting-very-strange-what-its-like-to-be-an-epidemiologist-right-now/ |access-date=January 19, 2021 |publisher=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |date=March 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817041955/https://www.chronicle.com/article/exhausting-very-strange-what-its-like-to-be-an-epidemiologist-right-now/ |archive-date=August 17, 2020}}</ref>
